The PanKbase Steering Committee is pleased to announce the following 2026 funding opportunities

Track 1 Collaborative Innovation Trainee Award

Award Overview

This track is designed to foster cross-center collaboration and innovative research among trainees. This award provides $100,000 in total costs to support a collaborative 1-year project between trainees from two PanKbase U24 centers.

Eligibility Requirements

  • Team composition: Applicant teams must include at least one trainee from each of the two U24 centers. Additional trainees can be included, but must be from an existing PanKbase site (including the 2025 OP fund awardee sites).
  • Time commitment: Awardees must dedicate a minimum of 50% FTE (full-time equivalent) protected time to the proposed project. Supervising PIs are required to cover this effort through cost-sharing, when needed, using the PI's PanKbase parent or sub-award budget.

Award Details

  • Funding amount: $100,000 total costs
  • Project duration:1 year
  • Conference travel support: Up to $5,000 per trainee for conference-related travel may be requested
  • Funding distribution: Funds will be distributed as a one-time increase of the subaward to trainees' respective PIs

Funding Structure

Awards will be distributed in two phases:

  • Phase 1: $50,000 TC for the first 6 months
  • Phase 2: Renewal for an additional $50,000 TC for the second 6 months, contingent upon satisfactory review of milestones and deliverables by NIDDK. NIDDK reserves the right to terminate components of the project or the project in its entirety if progress is deemed unsatisfactory.

Proposals should:

  • Describe an innovative, collaborative 1-year project
  • Clearly articulate quarterly milestones and deliverables (every 3 months) for both the overall project and each participating site.
  • Define clear outcome measures
  • Include plans to submit at least one abstract to a conference (provide names of target conferences; abstract submission may be included as a milestone)

Application Materials

Please submit a 1-2 page project description that addresses the requirements outlined above, together with 1-2 pages of milestones and deliverables; and bio-sketches of all key personnel. No need to include PIs’ bio-sketches.

Application due date:

July 15, 2026

Review and Selection

Proposals will be reviewed and selected by the PanKbase Steering Committee (SC), with emphasis on innovation and collaboration.

Earliest starting date:

August 15, 2026

Key dates

  • Full application due: July 15, 2026
  • Full application review by SC: July 24, 2026
  • Earliest project start date: August 15, 2026

Questions?

opfund@pankbase.org.

Track 2. PanKbase Capacity Building, Platform Enhancement, and Strategic Development Award

This funding opportunity will support up to two 1-yr projects at up to $200,000 in total costs each. Approximately $400,000 total is allocated to strengthen and expand the PanKbase program.

Award Purpose

This award is designed to:

  1. Fill critical gaps in the PanKbase program or develop high-value add-ons
  2. Enhance program infrastructure rather than pursue individual research interests
  3. Address unmet needs not already supported by the parent grant or covered by existing individual funding

Examples of fundable activities include (Please note that the examples listed are illustrative only and are not intended to be restrictive or exhaustive):

  • Gaps in documentation (standards, protocols, etc.)
  • Development of gap datasets
  • API wrappers and integration tools
  • New workflows, tools, or applications that enhance platform utility

Eligibility

  • All MPIs are eligible to apply
  • External collaborators: Not required but encouraged if they bring essential complementary expertise. External collaborators must be from an existing PanKbase site, including the sites of 2025 PanKbase OP fund awards.

Project Focus

Projects must be deliverable-driven, with tangible outputs such as (Please note that the examples listed are illustrative only and are not intended to be restrictive or exhaustive) :

  • Documentation and standards
  • New tools or applications
  • Workflows and pipelines
  • New datasets
  • Technical infrastructure improvements

Application Process

Step 1: Letter of Intent (LOI)

  • Length: Up to 1 page
  • Content: Describe the gaps being addressed and the added value of the proposed work
  • Due date: June 22, 2026

Step 2: Full Application (by invitation only)

  • SC LOI review: June 26, 2026
  • Invited applicants will submit:
    • 3 pages of science description
    • Supporting materials: bio-sketches of all key personnel and budget justification
  • Full application due date: August 17, 2026

Key dates

  • LOI due: June 22, 2026
  • LOI review by SC: June 26, 2026
  • Full application (by invitation only) due: August 17, 2026
  • Full application review by SC: August 28, 2026
  • Earliest project start date: September 1, 2026

Important Notes

  • Proposed work must not overlap with activities already supported by the parent grant or existing individual funding
  • Projects should demonstrate clear added value to the PanKbase program
  • Focus on collaborative capacity building and platform enhancement
  • Not for pursuing individual research interests

Questions?

opfund@pankbase.org.
